notes: Mirza Ghulam Ahmad takes the oath of allegiance at Ludhiana on 23 March 1889; followers gather in the United Provinces, the Punjab and Sindh.
The movement adopts the name Ahmadiyya in a manifesto of 4 November 1900.
After the death of Mirza Ghulam Ahmad, Hakeem Noor-ud-Din becomes the first Caliph (1908–1914).
The first organised overseas mission opens in Putney, London (1913).
Mirza Basheer-ud-Din Mahmood Ahmad becomes the second Caliph (1914–1965); a dissenting faction forms the Lahore Ahmadiyya Movement.
The second Caliph founds Rabwah in Pakistan after the partition of India (1948); under him missions reach 46 countries.
The third Caliph tours West Africa (1970) and sets up the Nusrat Jehan Scheme of schools and medical facilities.
The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation declares the Ahmadiyya not linked to Islam (1973).
After Pakistan promulgates Ordinance XX the fourth Caliph relocates to London (1984).
Mirza Masroor Ahmad is elected fifth Caliph in London (2003); by 2016 the Community is in 209 countries.
